pr.title: perf(prims-ts): QToken sparse group sizes 16 and 32 and a latency-model group policy for NVFP4 prefill
pr.body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Speeds up D256 Prims-TS QToken block-sparse attention with NVFP4 K/V for packed-query (prefill) calls. Follows #9375.

- **Group sizes 16 and 32.** Groups wider than 8 queries store page memberships in `ceil(G / 8)` page-major byte planes; queries `8p..8p+7` use plane `p`. Validation, workspace sizing, the metadata kernels and the Q128 KeepsMmaAb softmax read these planes.
  - G16/G32 require packed queries (`qo_indptr`), K/V fragments (`gcd(kv_block_size, page_size)`) of at most 16 tokens and the KeepsMmaAb recipe. `plan` rejects other configurations.
  - Their metadata keeps a map of the model's whole block prefix (`max_seq_len_kv / kv_block_size`) in shared memory. `plan` and workspace sizing reject a prefix whose map does not fit the device.
  - The membership tensor must have exactly `ceil(G / 8)` planes.
- **Group-size suggestion for NVFP4 K/V.** With `nvfp4_kv=True`, `suggest_q_token_kv_block_sparse_group_size` returns the G in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32} with the lowest modeled latency: `waves × (KV128 tiles per work item × tile cost + item cost) + metadata + split reduction`. A group's K/V tiles are estimated as `selected × G ** union_exponent`, capped at `seq_len_kv`. New optional arguments: `union_exponent`, `nvfp4_kv`, `seq_len_kv` and `packed_query`; G16/G32 are suggested only with `packed_query=True` and `kv_block_size <= 16`. With constants fitted on GB300, the suggested G is within 1.001× of the best explicit G on geomean and 1.04× in the worst case. BF16/FP8 caches keep main's coverage rule (G1–G8).
- **D256 recipe choice.** Raw BF16/FP8 caches and FP8 Q with NVFP4 K/V take SwapsMmaAb only for groups of at most 16 Q rows per KV head (Swaps Q32 trailed Keeps Q64 by 10–110%). Everything else keeps main's rules.
- **Grouped metadata.**
  - G9–G32 use a membership-entry map, which skips the separate membership pass, when the prefix fits without lowering occupancy; otherwise a bit map with an optional word-rank array.
  - When the warps divide the group's queries evenly, each warp enumerates one query.
  - G32 runs the bit-map kernel with 1024 threads (57 → 32 µs at 4K queries); G2–G4 keep four 512-thread CTAs per SM.
  - The packed-Q path issues the selected-block loads before route validation.
- **NVFP4 KeepsMmaAb loader, separate scales, grouped routes.** Several raw stages are kept in flight in registers, and the loader runs up to one tile further ahead. G1 routes and the interleaved-row layout are unchanged.
- **Docs.** `QTokenKvBlockSparsePagedTSWrapper.run` documents framework-side NVFP4 → BF16 conversion (see below). No conversion code is added.

### No-regression check against main

Every case was compared with main on GB300 with identical inputs. main and this PR alternate on one GPU (main, PR, main, PR), and a case counts as a regression when the PR's best run is more than 1% slower than main's worst. Heads 4/1, 16/2, 8/1, 2/1 and 1/1; prefix 0/32K/64K; 1–4096 packed queries with explicit G1–G8 and with the suggested G; fixed-Q decode with 64–512 requests at 8K/32K context and G1–G8.

| K/V cache | Q | Suggested G: geomean PR/main time | Cases |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| NVFP4, separate scales and interleaved rows | BF16 | 0.85 | 312 |
| NVFP4, separate scales and interleaved rows | FP8 | 0.85 | 312 |
| BF16 | BF16 | 0.94 | 156 |
| FP8 | FP8 | 0.96 | 156 |

No case regresses. G1 launches with at most 16 queries show end-to-end deltas of up to 1.4 µs in either direction; both trees launch the same kernels with the same grids and the same GPU span there.

FP8 Q with NVFP4 K/V (review question): for groups of at most 16 Q rows, Keeps vs Swaps depends on the scale layout, which `plan()` does not see. With more work items than SMs, Keeps is 13–17% faster with separate scale tensors but 2–12% slower with interleaved rows, and 2–5% slower for G1 decode in both layouts. The PR therefore keeps main's FP8 rule (Keeps from G5) and only adds the 16-row bound (Keeps Q64 was 2–26% faster than Swaps Q32 at 32 rows in every measured case).

### When a separate NVFP4 → BF16 K/V conversion pays in prefill

The kernel dequantizes NVFP4 K/V for every route that reads a tile, so overlapping routes repeat the work: at 4K queries over a 64K prefix, each selected token is dequantized about 90 times. A framework can instead convert each request's visible NVFP4 pages to a BF16 paged cache once per call and run the wrapper with `kv_dtype=torch.bfloat16`. This applies to BF16 Q only (FP8 Q rounds K/V to E4M3). Results are then bit-identical, since every E2M1 × E4M3 product is exact in BF16, and Prims-TS needs no change. Measured with a prototype on GB300 (D256, real indexer top-k, 512 blocks of 4 tokens, 0–64K prefixes):

- **Cost:** about 13 µs per 64K tokens per KV head (about 6.4 TB/s), plus a BF16 scratch cache of 3.6× the NVFP4 size (128 MB per request at 64K tokens × 2 KV heads).
- **Saving:** 1.45 µs per KV128 tile for TileQ128 groups (`group_size × Hq / Hkv > 64`) and 0.18 µs for 64-row tiles. It grows with the number of queries, not with context length.
- **Measured speedup vs the best NVFP4 launch:** 1.02–1.37× at 1K–4K queries, 0.84–1.11× at 512, 0.63–1.0× at 128–256.
- **Use it** for TileQ128 groups with at least 1K packed queries (512 at 8 Q heads per KV head) and contexts up to 64K.
- **Skip it** for 64-row tiles, fewer queries, memory-constrained deployments and unmeasured long contexts (at 1M tokens × 2 KV heads, conversion would take about 420 µs and 2 GB per request).
- **Gate fitted on 0–64K data:** convert when `(KV128 tiles / SMs) × per-tile saving > visible tokens × KV heads × 0.042 ns + 5 µs`, with a per-tile saving of 1.453 µs (Q128) or 0.179 µs (Q64).
- Converting only the selected blocks does not help: marking them costs more than it saves.
- When converting, pass `nvfp4_kv=False` to the group suggestion, and overlap the conversion with independent work such as the indexer top-k.

comments.body: Re the review-summary note on `QTokenKvBlockSparseUnionLaunchState::map_footprints` (one entry per model block bound): not changed. The key is `ceil(max_seq_len_kv / kv_block_size)`, a static planning parameter, so a process holds one entry per distinct (`max_seq_len_kv`, `kv_block_size`) pair it plans, per device and G16/G32 specialization. Each entry is a few bytes. Keying by footprint would save little and would still need the exact bound for the entry map.

Re CodeRabbit's outside-diff finding in review 5969314646 (plane spacing vs the widened per-head stride in `load_gmem_membership_word`): confirmed and fixed in c9d03ae7f. With `share_pattern_across_kv_heads=False`, nonpersistent CTAs widen the membership stride to Hkv rows, and the G9-G32 plane offset was derived from it, so queries 8+ read the next head's row. On GB300 the new per-KV-head cases (2 KV heads, Keeps Q64 and Q128) failed at query 8 on all six split-KV launches; persistent launches, which index rows without widening, passed. The resource now carries a plane stride computed once per CTA from the per-head row width, and both sites share one config property (`widens_sparse_metadata_rows_per_head`). All twelve cases pass, along with the full metadata (317) and decode (1207 passed, 96 skipped) suites.

**`prefers_nvfp4_keeps` changes the FP8-Q NVFP4 recipe for existing G1–G4 decode, untested and unmeasured**

```python
if q_dtype_key == "float8_e4m3fn":
    return rows > SWAPS_MAX_ROWS_D256 or num_routes * num_kv_heads > multi_processor_count
```

On main, FP8 Q took Keeps only for `group_size >= 5` or >32 rows. The route-count clause applies to every G, so it switches existing decode too. For example, FP8 Q with 4/1 heads at G1 and batch 200 on 148 SMs moves from Swaps to the FP8 Keeps transform, with 4 live rows in Q64.

- No QToken NVFP4 test reaches this clause with ≤16 rows. The `full-wave` cases have `routes * Hkv` equal to the SM count, not above it, and the wide-group test is BF16-Q only. The FP8 Keeps transform at G1 never runs.
- All performance tables in the description are BF16 Q. There is no FP8-Q data for this rule.

@qsang-nv Thanks, you were right on all three points: the routes clause changed existing FP8-Q decode, no test reached it, and there was no FP8 data. I measured it on GB300 with Keeps and Swaps forced in the same process with identical inputs (FP8 Q, NVFP4 K/V, both scale layouts; packed prefill with real indexer top-k, prefix 0/32K/64K, 1–4096 queries, heads 4/1, 16/2, 2/1, 1/1; fixed-Q decode with 32–512 requests at 8K–64K, G1–G8).

For groups of at most 16 Q rows the faster recipe depends on the scale layout, which `plan()` does not see:

| ≤16 rows | separate scale tensors | interleaved rows |
|---|---|---|
| more work items than SMs | Keeps 13–17% faster (G≥2, packed G1) | Swaps 2–12% faster |
| one wave or less | mixed | Swaps 2–10% faster |
| decode G1, 4/1 heads (your example) | Swaps 2–5% faster | Swaps 1–5% faster |

So the clause regressed interleaved rows (up to 15%) and G1 decode. ce6d4f60d drops it: FP8 Q with NVFP4 K/V keeps main's rule (Keeps from G5) and only adds the 16-row bound (at 32 rows Keeps Q64 was 2–26% faster than Swaps Q32 in every case). The G5–G8 small-head flip toward Swaps is gone with it.

I then checked the whole branch against main case by case (alternating main/PR runs on one GPU, all of BF16/FP8 Q × NVFP4 layouts, raw BF16 and FP8 caches, explicit and suggested G, fixed-Q decode) and fixed the other regressions this turned up; the commit message and the new "No-regression check against main" section list them. A layout-aware FP8 choice would need the layout at plan time, so I left it for a follow-up.
